sections.text: What Is Square Footage?
You hear 'square footage' every time you look at a house listing or buy flooring. It's just the area of a room measured in square feet. A **10x10 room** is **100 square feet**. Nothing fancy.

You'll see it everywhere — real estate listings, flooring orders, paint cans. Agents use it to price homes. Contractors use it to quote jobs. You'll use it when you're buying furniture, ordering carpet, or figuring out if that AC is strong enough for your living room.
The Square Footage Formula by Shape
The formula changes depending on what shape you're dealing with. Here are the three most common ones you'll run into.
Rectangle (Standard Rooms)
Most rooms are rectangles. Multiply length by width. That's it.
Rectangle Square Footage = Length × Width
Say you've got a **12x16 bedroom** — that's **192 sq ft**. A **10x10 room**? **100 sq ft**. Measure in feet, get square feet. Measure in meters, get square meters.
Measure wall to wall at the longest and widest points. Got a closet? Measure it separately and add it to the room total.
Circle (Round Rooms & Spaces)
Circular rooms aren't super common in homes, but they pop up in commercial spaces and fancier architecture. You'll need the radius (center to edge) and pi (π ≈ 3.14159).
Circle Square Footage = π × r²
Got a round dining area with an **8-foot radius**? That's π × 8² = **201 sq ft**. Only have the diameter? Cut it in half to get the radius.
L-Shaped Rooms
L-shaped rooms look complicated, but they're really not. Split the L into two rectangles, calculate each one, then add them together.
L-Shape Square Footage = (Length₁ × Width₁) + (Length₂ × Width₂)
Take a living room that's **18x14** with an attached dining area that's **10x8**: (18 × 14) + (10 × 8) = **332 sq ft**. Our calculator does this automatically, but it's good to know the logic.
Real-World Example: A Complete Home Project
So there you go. With a 10% waste factor (standard for LVP flooring), order **481 sq ft**. At **$4.50/sq ft**, that's **$2,163.65** in materials.
Why You Need a Waste Factor
Here's something that trips people up: you won't use every square foot you buy. Cuts, mistakes, damaged pieces — it adds up. That's why you need a waste factor.
Always round up to the nearest whole unit. A few extra square feet in the garage beats running out halfway through the job.
Measuring Tips for Accurate Results

items: Laser measurer: worth the $30, way more accurate than a tape measure.
Measure at multiple points. Walls are rarely perfectly straight.
Sketch a quick floor plan with dimensions labeled. Helps catch mistakes.
Include every section: closets, alcoves, bay windows.
Multi-story project? Measure each floor separately. They're never identical.

sections.text: Common Square Footage Questions
How many square feet is a 12×12 room?
A **12x12 room** is **144 sq ft**. Add 10% for waste and you're ordering **159 sq ft**.
How do I convert square feet to square meters?
Multiply sq ft by **0.092903** to get square meters. Going the other way? Multiply square meters by **10.7639**. Or just use the calculator — it does both for you.
